title: Ethiopian Fish Curry
community: Somali-influenced eastern Ethiopia — the fish curry of the lowlands
author: Chef Haile
desc: Ethiopian Fish Curry — fish simmered in an Ethiopian-spiced curry sauce with tomatoes, onion, turmeric, cardamom, and coriander. The curry format applied to Ethiopian lake fish, with berbere providing the unmistakably Ethiopian character.
longDesc: Ethiopian fish curry reflects the country's eastern lowland influence from Somali and Djiboutian food traditions — the curry format applied to freshwater fish. The berbere anchors it firmly in Ethiopian territory while the cardamom and coriander provide the curry complexity.
steps: Add garlic, ginger, berbere, turmeric, coriander, cardamom. Stir 1 minute.
Add tomatoes. Cook 6 minutes until thick.
Add water. Bring to a simmer.
Add fish fillets. Spoon sauce over.
chefTips: Do not stir once fish is added.
The sauce must be thick before adding fish — prevents watery result.
commonMistakes: Thin sauce when fish is added — fish releases water, making it thinner.
cookingScience: See ETH081 for fish wat science.
culturalNote: Ethiopian fish curry is the food culture of the eastern lowlands — where the highland teff and berbere tradition meets the coastal fish and spice traditions brought by Somali and Arab traders.
